meta.title: Retiring a Mount: Inventory to Delete, in Six Steps

views.label: Map before copying
views.note: Every dbutils.fs.mounts() path is mapped to a target external location or volume before any bytes move.

views.label: Rewrite before validating
views.note: Notebooks, jobs, and init scripts still point at the old path until this step runs.

views.label: Delete only after validation
views.note: Unmounting first is how a migration finds out what it missed the hard way.

cards.title: External locations are the DBFS-mount successor
items: An external location registers a cloud path with a storage credential, replacing dbfs:/mnt/
Volumes replace mounts for non-tabular files — libraries, config, images, raw exports
The identity mapping alone isn't enough; the target identity also needs an explicit grant on the target storage

cards.title: Rewrite before you validate
items: Every notebook, job, and init script referencing the old mount path needs updating
Validate file counts, checksums, and access permissions only after paths are rewritten
Skipping the rewrite step means validation passes against files nothing actually reads yet

cards.title: Unmount is the last step, not an early one
items: Delete source mounts only after verification — this is what avoids drift
An unmounted-too-early mount is a production incident, not a cleanup task
See target storage credentials for the identity this whole chain depends on
